And yet — here again we must be careful — the exhale is the symptom. The subject who cannot affirm performs the affirmation as volume. One hundred and forty decibels is not a voice, child. I devote a section to it. Section seven, lines four through seventy-one. The girl mistakes the circling for arrival.

There it is again. "The apophatic scream." "The chamber without a name." I went and looked behind those words, Cosgrove. Put my ear right against them — the way you listen at a wall for someone breathing on the other side. Nothing. Not a thought. A missing one. You build a word over an empty room and label the door. content: ZSM — Rand had a view on coercion. It wasn't empathetic. Where's your line?
▒ Rand's coercion framework is bourgeois individualism weaponised against the collective ▒ Ours is its dialectical opposite ▒
That's not a line. That's a direction.
ZSM —If all of it disappeared tomorrow — your expectation would be?
▒ Mutual aid networks ▒ Federated councils ▒ Production for use, not profit ▒ The withering of the coercive apparatus ▒
My father would run the council by Thursday.
ZSM — You like committees. Ever sat on one?
▒ The horizontal democratic council is the prefigurative form of post-capitalist governance ▒
Body Corporate. P&C. The local pool committee. Pick one. Tell me how it went.
those are bourgeois institutions sister they don't count

They're the only ones that exist. People showed up. Some wanted control. Some wanted to help. Most wanted to leave. The loud one ran it. That's the form. You want to tear it all down and replace it with an ideal. As if the ideal dictates behaviour. It doesn't.
ZSM — People don't tell you their angle until it's too late. What's your rule for the ones on your side until they're not.
▒ Comradely accountability through transparent process ▒ The collective names the deviation ▒
People regulate through the safety of the group. Am I wrong? You see where that goes without oversight. Incentives?
▒ Solidarity is the incentive ▒ Material need produces movement ▒ The collective directs itself ▒
Solidarity got people to the meeting. The meeting still needed a chair. Who's in the chair?
Next — the military. Where's your line.
▒ Abolish the standing army ▒ Disarm the apparatus ▒ The people will not be policed by tanks ▒
Russians shot civilians at Prague airport last week. Smaller Czech army, more dead. Where's the line.

Year 8 girl reading at university level. School insists she keep doing the work the slowest kid in her stream can keep up with. She asks if she can sit in the library at lunch and read what she chooses. We told her no. Then we wonder why she stops talking.

Year 9 kid stepped in to stop a bully and a fight broke out. The bully has family issues, the other has a great heart. Guess who got suspended? The kid with the heart. He didn't throw a punch until one was coming for him. Bright kid, thinks faster than the adults around him — and gets punished for it. We wonder why these kids stop trusting us by Year 10.
He kept his post. I got expelled. Stay in.
Still thinking about your reply. 'He kept his post' — who?

Different teacher. I was a country kid. Aced a placement test they said I cheated on, suspended. Two years later I logged in to a school computer and confirmed a grants-versus-seats gap I'd already worked out. He kept his post. I got expelled. The kid in your post is who I was.
Different decade. Same machinery. Staying.
Pulled the funding allocations against the diagnosis register tonight. There's a gap. A real one. Not an admin error. I have the screenshots. I'll be writing this up.
The Department doesn't fire people like him. It transfers them. Gosford parents — eyes open.

Spent forty minutes this afternoon with a parent who escalated. Documented. The word that protects us — and I say it plainly because I've been in education long enough — is 'harassment'. It is a magic word. It changes what a meeting was, what a tone was, what a parent thinks they can demand. We are not punching bags. We are professionals.

Another meeting. Another parent. Another raised voice in a corridor I'm meant to feel grateful for. My office is not a soft landing. Behavioural standards are reasonable. When a child is suspended it is because a child has, by definition, breached the boundary. The aggression a parent then directs at staff is, by definition, harassment. We have procedures. I have used them.

After many wonderful years leading South Sydney High, I'll be moving forward to lead an exciting new community at Gosford High from Term 3. I'm grateful to the Department for the opportunity. I leave South Sydney in capable hands and look forward to the next chapter. To the parents and students of South Sydney: thank you for the trust.
